$comment: Uptime monitors, kept in git rather than clicked into a dashboard, and applied by
`npm run monitors:sync`. A monitor that exists only in a vendor's UI is a monitor
nobody can review, nobody notices the deletion of, and nobody can recreate after an
account is lost — which is the same class of single-copy problem as the database.
Two checks, because they fail independently. `/health/live` is the one that matters:
the supervisor keeps the API up through a pipeline crash, so the site can serve a
dashboard that has quietly stopped advancing while every ordinary check stays green.
An ingest gap is permanent — NJT serves no history to backfill from.
`url` is overridden by NJT_PUBLIC_API_URL when set, so a staging deploy does not need
an edited copy of this file.

monitors.name: NJT API
monitors.comment: The site is reachable at all. Two minutes of confirmation before alerting, so a deploy or a machine restart does not page anyone.

monitors.name: NJT ingest
monitors.comment: 503 once TripUpdates has been silent for an hour. Checked every five minutes rather than every thirty seconds: the condition it reports changes on the scale of an hour, and polling it faster only adds requests.
